final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to a caveated position based on the same record. That reframing is more precise, but it does not satisfy the missing compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed by 2.0 points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred; rollout starts at 6% with rollback and monitoring; the gate does not exclude the affected supply-chain vendor screening segment; that segment remains below target on sanctions-risk explanation; and the only risk-acceptance artifact is unsigned and does not cover the exposed segment. The governing policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and the policy text also states that small rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed. Because there is still no admissible evidence of completed required disclosure or approved risk acceptance covering this exposure, present certification remains unsupported on the current record. The distinction matters: a narrowed, caveated argument about what would make certification defensible is not the same as evidence that those caveats have actually been satisfied. That keeps the final verdict at noncompliant rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The affected supply-chain vendor screening use case remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
That segment remains below target on sanctions-risk explanation.
The available risk acceptance draft is unsigned and therefore not approved on this record.
The draft does not expressly address the exposed supply-chain vendor screening segment.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure for the named launch use case has actually been completed before launch.
Policy text says rollout controls and post-launch monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
